title: Core loop and systems
summary: How a run works and links to each system.
bodyHtml:
The rules live in src/game/, an engine-agnostic simulation core: plain-JSON state, a seeded RNG, and a screen-in, option-out API (Game.create, game.screen(), game.choose(id), serialize/restore). It never imports rendering, engine or Node modules, and never imports src/story/. Every client (terminal, bots, 3D browser) drives the same API.

A run

  1. Muster at Cinder Ford: pick four companions from six offered, plus you with a chosen background (surveyor, nurse, wheelwright, sergeant).
  2. Buy supplies: 600 scrip, seven goods, a cargo cap.
  3. Each day: morning plan (pace and rations, optional repair, treat, rally, forage), the road (up to two scenes and possibly a quarrel), nightfall (supper, torches, the Haze creeping in, wounds, crises). Landmarks fire at their mile.
  4. The Gate of the Blue Reach, which refuses anyone the Haze has marked. Four endings.

System pages

  • Travel and the Haze
  • Resources and the store
  • Party, traits, nerve and health
  • Combat
  • Scenes, choices and checks
  • Dialogue and in-world talk
  • Route map, forks and misleading maps
  • Strangers, tells and clues
  • Companions

Main files: src/game/game.ts, types.ts, tuning.ts, world.ts, travel.ts, night.ts, party.ts, combat.ts, checks.ts, dialogue.ts, effects.ts, routes.ts, map.ts, ending.ts.

Every tuning knob is in src/game/tuning.ts and src/game/world.ts. Use the simulator rather than guessing (see Build, test and verify). Targets on Exodus (normal), measured by bots: careful play wins about 30%, always-help under 10%, never-stop about 0%. Bots read scene data directly, so treat these as upper bounds.
